title: Hybrid weekly + LTS staggered cut pipeline and release-note synthesizer
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: Replace the brittle weekly monolithic cut job with a hybrid pipeline that supports staggered regional slices, integrates LTS coldfix lanes, and generates an automated, human-readable release-note draft (synthesizer) that groups changes by customer-impact and subsystem. Scope includes: (1) cut pipeline orchestration (slice scheduler + RC tagging rules), (2) canary and SLO-driven gating for each slice, (3) LTS coldfix lane integration to allow out-of-band patches onto the LTS channel without disrupting the weekly cadence, and (4) a release-note synthesizer service that compiles PR diffs, notable commits, and changelog fragments into a single draft with suggested sections for the docs/marketing teams.
acceptance_criteria: Cut pipeline can run a weekly master cut that produces 3 staggered regional RC slices (us, eu, ap) with independent tagging and rollouts
If a critical LTS hotfix is present, the LTS lane is emitted as an out-of-band RC and does not stop the weekly master cut
Canary gating hook rejects a slice if the canary SLO regression >= 3%% at 95%% confidence or if error rate increases by 20%% over baseline
Automated release-note draft is produced within 15 minutes of final RC tagging and includes: grouped change sections, linked PRs, highlighted breaking changes, and suggested user-facing blurb
Documentation and runbook updated with step-by-step rollback and manual-cut procedure and tested in staging with a dry-run
implementation_plan: Design: finalize slice scheduler semantics and RC tag naming convention (ENG + region + LTS flag)
Infra: add slice job runner in shipline that can allocate cut workers to region-specific queues
Gating: implement SLO-driven webhook that evaluates canary metrics and returns pass/fail; include confidence estimation
LTS lane: allow merges labeled 'lts/coldfix' to be collected and emitted as separate RCs with dependency pinning
Release-note synthesizer: create a lambda that aggregates merged PR metadata, diff heuristics, and changelog fragments; generate markdown with sections and suggested tweets/announcements
Testing: run three staged dry-runs in staging with synthetic canaries, validate gating, and iterate
Rollout: enable opt-in for a small set of services for the next two weekly cuts, then flip to default after metrics validation
risks: Automated gating thresholds may be too sensitive leading to excessive cut rejections — mitigated by tuning and a manual override window
Release-note synthesizer may misclassify PRs or omit context — require a two-step human review before publish
Increased complexity of staggered slices could cause unexpected cross-region dependency issues for infra deployments
Edge cases where LTS coldfixes depend on non-LTS changes could complicate out-of-band RC creation
notes: Design decision 2026-02-25: use tag format rc/<YYYY>.<WEEK>-<region>-<slice-id> and append +lts for LTS RCs
Trade-off: we accept a small scheduling lag (up to 30 minutes) to allow cross-region KV cache warmups before canary asserts
Benchmarks: a dry-run produced RC artifacts in 9 minutes on average for small services and 18 minutes for large-model services
Related docs: linking to runbooks and console dashboard mockups (confluence: /release-infra/staggered-cuts)
